name: Partial Cubes Are Recognizable with Coordinates in Quadratic Time
statement: An arbitrary $n$-vertex graph can be tested for being a partial cube in $O(n^2)$ word-RAM time. On acceptance, the same algorithm outputs an isometric hypercube labelling with one coordinate for each $\Theta$-class.
proof: Breadth-first distance data identify candidate semicube cuts and the algorithm verifies the partial-cube cut partition while incrementally assigning one bit per accepted cut. Failure of a cut or distance condition rejects the graph; when all cuts pass, Hamming distance in the constructed labels equals graph distance. The data structures and total scans take quadratic word-RAM time.
comments: The full coordinate output can itself require quadratic size, for example on paths.
